resources.string: A lightweight iperf2/iperf3 client for quick TCP/UDP throughput checks.
Write every argument in the command itself (-c host, -p port, -t duration, …).
Invalid custom command (check that quotes are balanced)
Duration must be between 1 and 86400 seconds
Bandwidth must be between 1 and 100000 Mbps
⚠️ Port %1$s is the default port of %2$s, but the current engine is %3$s — make sure both ends match on engine/port/protocol (peer: `iperf3 -s`↔iperf3, `iperf -s`↔iperf2).
Server address %1$s points at this device itself — this app cannot be its own server here; enter the peer device\'s IP.
Server address %1$s is this phone\'s own address (see the IP shown at the top). A client must target the peer machine running the server.
[Port %1$s is in use — this run uses port %2$s instead. Point the peer client at -p %2$s.]
Port %1$s is already in use — add -p %2$s to your command to use a free port.
Port %1$s is already in use by another program on this phone — stop it or use a different port.
Put a %1$s binary built for this device\'s architecture at assets/%2$s and reinstall.
%1$s executable not found — add assets/%2$s and reinstall. Original error: %3$s
Connection refused (nothing is listening on that port).
The peer did not speak iperf3\'s protocol — the server may be running iperf2 (`iperf -s`) or something else; use the same iperf generation on both ends
Connection timed out (check the address / port / network reachability)
No route to host (possibly a different network)
Could not resolve the server address
The server is busy (another test is running)
Could not connect to the server
Communication with the server failed (engine or port mismatch?)
The connection to the server closed unexpectedly
Connection broken: write failed (engine mismatch with the server?)
iperf3 reported an error (see the log)
Hint: make sure both ends match on ① engine (peer: `iperf3 -s`↔iperf3, `iperf -s`↔iperf2) ② port (iperf3 defaults to 5201, iperf2 to 5001) ③ TCP/UDP (an iperf2 server needs `-u` to accept UDP)
Hint: iperf3\'s -u (UDP), -b, … are client-only options — an iperf3 server takes just `-s` and the connecting client decides TCP/UDP; to keep iperf2\'s `-u -s` habit switch the engine to iperf2
Hint: that option is iperf3-server-only — remove it from the client command
Hint: the peer did not answer this engine\'s protocol — it may be running the other iperf generation; use the same one on both ends (peer: `iperf3 -s`↔iperf3, `iperf -s`↔iperf2)
